title: Paper Tour script
description: A narrated walkthrough of one paper. Steps refer to doc.json elements by ID only, never by coordinates; the player resolves IDs to rects. A hand-written tour and an LLM-written tour use the same format.

paper.description: Folder name of the paper under demo/, e.g. "attention".

doc_sha256.description: source.sha256 of the doc.json this tour was written against.

voices.description: Voice settings per speaker name. Steps whose speaker has no entry use the default voice.

preset.description: Length the tour was written for: quick (about 6 steps), standard (about 10-12) or deep (up to 24).

suggested_questions.description: Questions offered to the learner when the tour ends.

part.description: What is missing: the whole step, its own explanation (a short summary stands in), its worked example, its side board or pen marks.

cause.description: Why: the model took too long, what it wrote failed the checks, its answer could not be used, it would have repeated earlier content, or the model could not be reached.

because.description: A step that went whole because its worked example could not be written and it was nothing without it.

left_out.description: What the writer planned but left out of this tour, and why. Absent when nothing was left out; the reader says so when the tour starts and ends.

doc_type.description: The kind of document, so the reader can pick its mode; a lecture deck plays slide by slide.

name_hint.description: Substring of a preferred browser voice name, e.g. "Samantha".

say.description: Narration. Words are counted by splitting on whitespace; at_word indexes into that list.

hold_ms.description: Pause after the narration before the next step.

audio.description: Pre-rendered narration. When absent, the player speaks `say` with the browser's speech synthesis.

word_times_ms.description: Start time of each word of `say`.

checkpoint.description: A pause where the learner tries first: the step asks, hints come one at a time, and the next step reveals the answer.

prompt.description: What the learner should try, in one or two sentences.

hints.description: Up to three hints, from a nudge to almost the answer.

targetId.description: Any doc.json ID: block (p3.b2), sentence (p3.s12), section (sec-3.2), figure or table (fig1, tab2), panel (fig2.a), equation (eq1), or a whole page (page4).

region.description: Sub-area of the target, normalized to the target's bbox: [x0, y0, x1, y1] with 0 to 1 values. Use it to point inside a figure when no panel ID fits.

atWord.description: Fire when narration reaches this word index of `say`. 0 = at step start.

persist.description: Keep this overlay on screen after the step ends, until a `clear` action.

oneOf.description: Move the camera so the target is in view at reading zoom (page width fits the viewport).
Move and zoom the camera so the target (or a region of it) fills the viewport.

padding.description: Margin around the target as a fraction of its size.

oneOf.description: Marker-style highlight that hugs the text lines of each target.
Outline around the target or a region of it, with an optional label.
Dim everything except the target or a region of it.
Callout card next to the anchor. Supports **bold** and `code` only.
Remove all persistent overlays.
A hand-drawn arrow pointing at the target or a region of it, with an optional short label at its tail.

from.description: The side the arrow comes from.

oneOf.description: A hand-drawn circle around the target or a region of it, with an optional short label.
Show an item on the side board, replacing the one before. It stays until another board item or board_clear, also across steps.
Light up a formula term, flow node, bar, curve (then plot mark), scene object, heatmap row, scatter point, shapes matrix, timeline event (then span) or distribution (then its region) by index.
Remove the item from the side board.

boardItem.description: Native board content. Timed board actions define successive states, including a general scene of positioned mathematical objects.

oneOf.description: A formula built term by term. Every term is a substring of latex and keeps its colour.
Boxes and arrows of a pipeline or architecture, revealed in order.
Bars that animate numbers reported in the document.

x_scale.description: A log axis needs a range above zero.

source.description: document only when the expressions are the document's own; a plot is illustrative otherwise.

marks.description: Facts the code finds on the curves and draws as labelled points: a root, an extremum, a crossing of two curves, a value at a stated x.

which.description: extremum: the highest or lowest point.

nth.description: root or crossing: counted from the left.

at.description: value: the x whose value is read.

points.description: Measured points from the document, drawn over the curves.

text.description: Required readable content for text/math objects; math text supports LaTeX. Shapes may use text as their own label, avoiding a separate overlapping text object.

plotId.description: Bind arrow/vector/circle to this plot object using data coordinates. Arrow/vector x,y start and w,h are signed endpoint deltas. Circle x,y is its LOWER-LEFT bounding corner; w,h are positive diameters, so center (u,v) needs x=u-w/2,y=v-h/2.

oneOf.description: A grid of values with labelled rows and columns. The values are always present; an expression, when given, is how they were computed (x is the column number, a the row number, both from 1).

normalize.description: The values are raw scores; the board shows a row-wise softmax turning each row into weights that sum to one.

mask.description: Square grids only: cells above the diagonal are masked.

oneOf.description: Points on two measured axes, such as quality against cost.

better.description: The corner where results are better.

series.description: Points of one series are joined in order; at most 3 series.

oneOf.description: How the dimensions of matrices combine through an operation: matrix, operator, matrix, ..., ending with a matrix.

label.description: The function applied by apply, such as softmax.

oneOf.description: Events, spans and deadlines on one axis. Every position is computed from the dates, offsets and lengths the document states: days from the anchor (from the first date without one), or the step on a step axis.

origin.description: The date at position 0, when the board has dates.

after.description: The label of an event, or of the anchor, this is measured from.

position.description: Computed: where it falls, in days from the anchor (steps on a step axis).

oneOf.description: One or two distributions drawn from their parameters (or from counts the document prints); the board morphs from the first to the second. The shaded region's chances are computed.

probabilities.description: Computed: the chance of the range under each distribution, in order.

objective.description: What the reader should understand from the visible mathematical change.

code.description: A JavaScript function expression receiving {t,params,data,theme,math,svg}. t is 0..1 and follows speech. Return svg.scene(content), an SVG string. Use the documented drawing/math helpers, loops and your own functions; no imports, DOM, fetch or independent timers. The runtime executes only isolated WebAssembly.

figure.description: Plotly figure JSON with data and layout. Allowed traces: scatter, bar, heatmap, contour, scatter3d, surface. Include labeled axes/units and exactly sourced measurements. No HTML, URLs, images, scripts or external resources.

expression.description: Bounded arithmetic expression using x, a, and sin/cos/tanh/exp/log/sqrt. a is the interactive parameter.
